posts.title: Guishan Lingyun Temple (龜山靈雲寺哲學廟)
posts.description: Lingyun Temple (靈雲寺) is an idiosyncratic house of worship in the hills of Tukeng Village (兔坑里), Guishan. It was founded in the early 1990s by Hsieh Shih-te (謝石德), an illiterate native of Lugu in Nantou, born in 1920, who devised his own teachings from Buddhism, Daoism, Confucianism, Christianity, and Taiwanese folk religion. posts.title: Lukang Wuze Temple (鹿港杉行街武澤宮)
posts.description: After dark on Shanhang Street. Wuze Temple is neighbourhood shrine on Shanhang Street (杉行街) in Lukang, which is named for the merchants who once traded in Fujian fir along this laneway leading to Lungshan Temple. posts.title: Eighteen Arhats Cave (十八羅漢洞)
posts.description: A cave temple damaged in a typhoon, sealed with bricks, and abandoned. In the early 2020s it was broken open and it became popular with urban explorers. The interior is dangerous and appropriate precautions should be taken.
